entries.label: home
entries.reason: A premises of homes holds one dwelling for each 50 m2 of the floor its premises record states, at least one, and a dwelling houses two residents; nobody works there and nobody visits. A default with its source, replaceable by a world's own value, never a census claim: Table 1 of "Technical housing standards: nationally described space standard" (Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government, published 27 March 2015) gives 50 m2 as the minimum gross internal floor area of a one bedroom, two person, one storey dwelling (row "1b 2p 50 58 1.5"); read 2026-10-10 at https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/technical-housing-standards-nationally-described-space-standard/technical-housing-standards-nationally-described-space-standard, a publication "licensed under the terms of the Open Government Licence v3.0 except where otherwise stated". A premises record's floor area is the building's storeys, walls and shared stairs included, which the standard's figure leaves out, so the default counts more dwellings than a surveyor would.
